principles: Only fix the real correctness gap: row-level parallelism must not corrupt evidence.
Do not optimize arbitrarily: add optional shard controls without changing serial experiment semantics.
Keep logic consistent with Proofbound host-neutral architecture: hosts run shards, Proofbound validates keys and evidence.
Fail closed on duplicates, missing keys, digest drift, invalid shard indexes, or concurrent same-shard writers.
drivers: B-991d runner files are not yet merged into canonical main.
Current side conversation cannot use subagents or provider execution.
The implementation must be verifiable with local dry-run/fixture tests only.

options.name: Patch B-991d run-full directly
pros: Could immediately affect B-991d if manually copied
cons: The file is not in this worktree or canonical main
Would conflict with active B-991d evidence work
Risk of touching ongoing provider execution

options.name: Add canonical Cell03 shard helper package
pros: Does not touch active B-991d rows
Can be validated locally without provider calls
Reusable when B-991d runner is merged
Keeps protocol semantics separate from execution hosts
cons: Requires a later small integration step for the live B-991d runner

chosen: Add canonical Cell03 shard helper package
rationale: The canonical helper solves the correctness gap without editing unmerged B-991d runner files or active evidence, and it gives the future runner a tested shard/merge contract.

preMortem.scenario: Shard plan misses or duplicates a cell key
preMortem.trigger: Enumeration differs from the frozen Cell03 expected-key rule
preMortem.consequence: Parallel execution can silently skip or duplicate formal rows
preMortem.mitigation: Selfcheck asserts all 1,152 expected keys are covered exactly once across shards.

preMortem.scenario: Two runners write the same shard
preMortem.trigger: A stale or missing lock is ignored
preMortem.consequence: Shard rows contain duplicate attempts that pollute merge input
preMortem.mitigation: Use mkdir lock per shard and selfcheck the second acquisition fails closed.

preMortem.trigger: Prompt/tool/task digest or shard count drift is not compared
preMortem.consequence: Rows from different protocols are treated as one experiment
preMortem.mitigation: Merge requires identical manifest binding fields and rejects digest drift.
